title: "3. Which of the 25 predictions should you keep?"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
jupyter: python3
---

Every variant produces 25 predictions per target (5 seeds x 5 diffusion
samples). The pipeline must publish one of them using a rule that does not see
the reference structure. Selecting the lowest-RMSD prediction is an oracle. It
needs the answer, so it cannot run on a novel target and it overstates what a
pipeline delivers. This document measures how much of that ceiling a
reference-free rule recovers.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

d = load()
pred = d["pred"]
```

## Selection rules compared

```{python}
def pick_ok(g, col, ascending=False):
    gg = g.dropna(subset=[col])
    if not len(gg):
        return np.nan
    i = gg[col].idxmin() if ascending else gg[col].idxmax()
    return bool(gg.loc[i, RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD)


rows = []
for (m, f, pdb), g in pred.groupby(["model", "msa", "pdb"]):
    g = g.copy()
    for c in ["plddt", "iptm", "ptm", "ranking_score"]:
        g["r_" + c] = g[c].rank(pct=True)
    g["rank_avg"] = g[["r_plddt", "r_iptm", "r_ptm", "r_ranking_score"]].sum(axis=1)
    frac = (g[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).mean()
    rows.append({
        "model": m, "msa": f, "pdb": pdb,
        "oracle (lowest RMSD)": bool(g[RA_COL].min() < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD),
        "avg pLDDT": pick_ok(g, "plddt"),
        "ipSAE": pick_ok(g, "ipsae_min"),
        "lowest mean PAE": pick_ok(g, "pae_mean", ascending=True),
        "AF ranking score": pick_ok(g, "ranking_score"),
        "pTM": pick_ok(g, "ptm"),
        "ipTM": pick_ok(g, "iptm"),
        "rank-average of all four": pick_ok(g, "rank_avg"),
        "consensus (modal pose)": bool(frac > 0.5),
        "_arbitrary": frac,
    })
sel = pd.DataFrame(rows)

RULES = ["oracle (lowest RMSD)", "avg pLDDT", "ipSAE", "lowest mean PAE",
         "AF ranking score", "pTM", "ipTM", "rank-average of all four",
         "consensus (modal pose)"]
ceiling = sel["oracle (lowest RMSD)"].mean()
summary = pd.DataFrame([
    {"rule": r, "targets posed correctly": f"{100 * sel[r].mean():.1f}%",
     "% of oracle ceiling": f"{100 * sel[r].mean() / ceiling:.1f}%",
     "reference-free?": "no" if r.startswith("oracle") else "yes"}
    for r in RULES])
summary.loc[len(summary)] = ["arbitrary single prediction",
                             f"{100 * sel['_arbitrary'].mean():.1f}%",
                             f"{100 * sel['_arbitrary'].mean() / ceiling:.1f}%",
                             "yes"]
summary
```

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.6))
vals = [100 * sel[r].mean() for r in RULES]
cols = ["#999999" if r.startswith("oracle") else "#0072B2" for r in RULES]
order = np.argsort(vals)
ax.barh(np.arange(len(RULES)), [vals[i] for i in order],
        color=[cols[i] for i in order], edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6)
ax.axvline(100 * sel["_arbitrary"].mean(), ls="--", color="#D55E00", lw=1.4)
ax.text(100 * sel["_arbitrary"].mean(), -0.7, " arbitrary pick", color="#D55E00",
        fontsize=9, va="top")
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(RULES)))
ax.set_yticklabels([RULES[i] for i in order], fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel("% of (model, target) pairs posed correctly")
save_fig(fig, "selection_rule_comparison")
plt.show()
```

- Average pLDDT is the best reference-free rule. It is the strongest single
  score even though the task is interface placement.
- Combining scores does not help. The rank-average of all four lands at or below
  the best single metric, so the interface measures add noise rather than signal
  for this decision.
- Consensus performs worse than an arbitrary pick. Taking the modal pose loses
  decisively to confidence selection, because a model biased towards the wrong
  interface sends most of its 25 samples there. Majority voting then amplifies
  the bias instead of cancelling it. Consensus needs independent errors, and
  these errors are systematically correlated.

## Head to head, and what each rule leaves on the table

```{python}
best_rule = "avg pLDDT"
head = []
for r in ["ipTM", "consensus (modal pose)", "AF ranking score"]:
    head.append({"rule": r,
                 f"{best_rule} right, this wrong": int((sel[best_rule] & ~sel[r]).sum()),
                 f"this right, {best_rule} wrong": int((~sel[best_rule] & sel[r]).sum())})
pd.DataFrame(head)
```

```{python}
recoverable = int(sel["oracle (lowest RMSD)"].sum())
pd.DataFrame([
    {"rule": r,
     "recoverable cases missed":
         int((sel["oracle (lowest RMSD)"] & ~sel[r]).sum()),
     "of recoverable": recoverable}
    for r in ["avg pLDDT", "ipTM", "AF ranking score", "consensus (modal pose)"]])
```

## Per-model breakdown

```{python}
per = (sel.groupby(["model", "msa"])
          .agg(**{"oracle": ("oracle (lowest RMSD)", "mean"),
                  "avg pLDDT": ("avg pLDDT", "mean"),
                  "ipTM": ("ipTM", "mean")})
          .mul(100).round(0).astype(int).reset_index())
per["combo"] = [combo_label(m, f) for m, f in zip(per["model"], per["msa"])]
per[["combo", "oracle", "avg pLDDT", "ipTM"]].sort_values("oracle", ascending=False)
```

- pLDDT wins or ties in almost every combination. Boltz-2 without an MSA is the
  exception, where ipTM edges it.
- The gap between the oracle column and the rest is the cost of not knowing the
  answer. It is the main caveat on every accuracy figure in this benchmark.

## What the pipeline does

`compute_metrics.py` publishes one representative structure per model into
`best_models/`, selected on highest average pLDDT.

Where an intended pose exists, as in an RFDiffusion design, select on RMSD to
that pose instead. The oracle rule is legitimately available there. Selecting a
design because it matches the requested pose is circular as evidence of binding,
so pair it with an interface check.
